Unless you really like frustration and lack of information as to why things aren't working, I'd steer clear of this for now. Maia's concept basically takes Dwarf Fortress and puts it into space, on another planet. That's both a good and a bad thing. Like DF, you decide what needs to get done, and the colonists go off and do that on their own, with no direct control. Unlike DF, if a colonist is unable to do something, you don't actually get any sort of message as to why — it just doesn't get done. It could be that (judging by the progress speed that makes continental drift seem fast) in half a decade it will evolve into the most amazing colony sim ever. Or not. Who knows? Ridiculous amount of potential but so poorly executed that it just becomes frustrating. I have tried and tried with this game through bugs and crashes and more. It is such a creative, fun and brilliant idea but its just not there in the gameplay. I find myself turning this off after an hour at a time because I get too frustrated. You have no direct control over your 'settlers' so you simply tell them what to build and where. Unfortunately you will find a group of 8 people that are starving to death would rather run around repairing items (even when you have an automated repair bot) than building places to grow seeds, cultivate them and then cook them. They will have beds but die of fatigue.

I loved medieval dynasty and had high expectations for this game and was really looking forward to it due to my love for the wild west. Over the 4 hours that I played I ran into various game breaking bugs that crashed the game just by opening UI, a lot of quests I had to restart the game to progress through or completely start a new save file because of those bugs bugging out the current save. Overall I can't recommend it especially for the price that it is... if anything I would of released this as a early access demo

The developers were given the huge task of bringing a game like Medieval Dynasty to the wild west but they failed so so bad. The first attempt was so bad it had to be rewritten and in Jan 2024 they decided to start over with a new character and new story-line. The early access version was not optimized, was horribly riddled with bugs and while the premise of the story was decent it never got the chance to be fully fleshed-out. This game has a TON of potential. I love survival games and I'm fascinated with anything to do with the Old West. I played it when it first released. Very buggy, as I knew it would be. So I took about a year hiatus to let the devs cook, then came back. After a year you can tell they have made some progress, but not nearly what I had hoped for. There are still a TON of issues, both visually and mechanically. Like some other reviews, it should not have left early access. I really enjoy the concept, but it's still just missing so much. Guess I'll try again in another year or so. Maybe.

Rumors suggest that the real issue might be with the publisher, TinyBuild, as there are claims that the developers are stuck in a restrictive contract. If these rumors are true, it's a big red flag not just for this game but for all TinyBuild-published titles. I strongly recommend saving your money and considering Starbound instead. Game is unplayable in current state. Parts of the map load visibly but not with physics, so you'll be walking along and then fall to your death through what should be solid ground. To make it more fun, it changes between game loads, so if you venture out and walk on something you didn't build, you're playing Russian roulette with every step. I am probably going to finish this game though I don't recommend it. I am merely doing it to honor the classic Sword and Fairy Inn (original). This one is more like an idle clicker mobile games. The story line is boring. Many mechanics and features also feels early access. I am a fan of Softstar as they had so many classics, but this is just not up to standard. It feels like they are just making money off the lore. I sad.

Extremely boring and repetitive, devs also removed the Exploration feature from Sword and Fairy Inn 1. From repetitive dating event dialogue, lack of actual restaurant management features, to the intentional slow pace of event progression to drag out the game (a single short story event gets broken up into a few lines of dialogue per day). This has all the skeleton and skins of a restaurant simulation game with no soul. I played 26 hours and just couldn't bring myself to finish the game cuz its so fking boring.
